title: Mockup Creation in Photoshop: Three-Phase Workflow with Generative AI, Smart Objects, and Realistic Lighting
summary: PHLEARN's Day 26 tutorial demonstrates building a realistic poster mockup in Photoshop through a three-phase workflow. Phase 1 cleans the background by removing unwanted graphics using the Generative AI Remove tool on a new layer, including careful text removal to keep lighting intact. Phase 2 constructs a non-perspective base for the mockup by extracting a billboard’s size with a polygonal Lasso, filling and transforming a white rectangle, then converting it into a Smart Object for non-destructive editing and easy updates. Phase 3 adds realism by duplicating the background into a new layer, applying it as a clipped, soft-light overlay to the mockup, and tweaking with Apply Image, clipping masks, and Levels to replicate shadows and highlights. The session also covers updating inside the smart object in real time, and using Generative Fill to populate the design (e.g., clouds) while maintaining perspective consistency.

sections.title: Phase 1: Background cleanup with Generative AI Remove Tool
sections.description: The presenter begins with the background image, enabling the Generative AI Remove Tool on a new layer. He highlights unwanted objects (e.g., foreground figure, text) and uses the tool to remove them, iterating on removal and refinements. The process emphasizes preserving light sources to maintain realism and demonstrates brush sizing via brackets, then groups the removals into a named layer called 'remove'.

sections.title: Phase 2: Build and convert a mockup surface as a Smart Object
concepts: Lasso tool (polygonal) to trace billboard silhouette
Fill with white and transform into a regular rectangle
Convert to Smart Object for non-destructive editing
Masking to reveal the clean billboard area
Editing inside the Smart Object and applying updates
sections.description: A new white shape is created to represent the billboard, derived from a perspective-corrected trace. The shape is converted to a Smart Object to enable editing in a separate file, with the ability to resize and reposition while preserving the original. The artist creates a layer mask by selecting the original billboard, inverting the selection, and painting with black to hide the old content. The process highlights using Smart Objects for efficient updates and ongoing edits.

sections.title: Phase 3: Realistic integration with lighting and perspective
concepts: Apply Image to capture lighting from the base image
Clipping mask to constrain lighting to the mockup
Soft Light blending to integrate highlights/shadows
Saving and updating smart objects to propagate changes
Generative Fill for asset augmentation (e.g., clouds)
sections.description: Phase 3 focuses on integrating the mockup with realistic lighting. A snapshot of the base image is applied via Apply Image to generate a layer of highlights and shadows, then clipped to the billboard via a clipping mask. The layer uses Soft Light blending to blend with the mockup, and Levels are used to fine-tune darks, lights, and midtones. The workflow emphasizes saving the Smart Object to see live updates in the composition and demonstrates Generative Fill for adding cloud assets to enhance realism. The session ends with advice on maintaining two-dimensional design constraints for perspective-mconsistent results.
